title: Power Automate process mining: import star schema (normalised) event data
notes: claim 58: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the Fabric automation shown only lists tenant settings; it cannot configure the OneLake access control beside it. The Fabric navigation also starts inside the Govern section rather than showing how to reach it. The import description and published licensing quantities are supported.

claims.claim: Process Mining can ingest a star schema rather than requiring a single wide table.

claims.claim: OneLake/Fabric and Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 are supported sources for normalized import.
claims.quote: OneLake / Microsoft Fabric: A lakehouse with managed Delta tables, or loose Parquet or CSV files under the Files/ area. Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2: A container with CSV, Parquet, or Delta-Parquet folders.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licence specific to normalized import is named in the product licensing or feature articles.
claims.quote: Searched: "normalized" "process mining" capacity licensing billing. Read normalized UX and authoring guides, process-advisor-overview licensing and prerequisites, and Power Platform licensing FAQs process-mining sections. General Power Automate licences are named, not a separate import licence.

claims.claim: No price or separate meter specific to normalized import is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "normalized" "process mining" capacity licensing billing; Power Automate normalized schema import licensing capacity price meter scheduled incremental refresh default. Read normalized guides, overview and licensing FAQs: no separate import meter.

claims.claim: Stored process data mostly uses Dataverse file capacity and a larger import can exhaust Dataverse storage.
claims.quote: Depending on the size of the process data you import, you might run out of Dataverse storage capacity. ... The process data we store uses mostly file capacity.

claims.claim: The articles do not explain how normalized-import data is counted against process mining capacity or Dataverse file capacity.
claims.quote: Searched: "normalized" "process mining" capacity licensing billing. Read normalized UX and authoring articles, process-advisor-overview capacity text and licensing FAQs. General stored-data capacity applies; no normalized-schema accounting calculation or treatment is stated.

claims.claim: Customers can assess highest monthly Process Mining usage using current and past usage data in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Yes, customers can assess their highest monthly Process Mining usage to understand capacity needed. Current and past usage data are available in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, second bullet

claims.claim: Other users and administrators see no change from normalized import.
claims.quote: Searched: "normalized" "process mining" "disable"; "normalized" "process mining" API PowerShell pac table entity. Read both normalized-import guides and security article. They document maker import and process access, not a guarantee that other users or administrators see no change.
claims.fix: Remove '; other users and administrators see no change' from the impact rationale, leaving 'Low. Makers and analysts who build process mining models from lakehouse data notice it.'

claims.claim: Normalized import requires an environment with Process Mining enabled and an account with rights to create processes.
claims.quote: A Power Automate environment where Process Mining is enabled, and a user account with rights to create processes in it.

claims.claim: Dataverse security roles govern access to process mining features.
claims.quote: The process mining capability relies on environment security and Microsoft Dataverse security roles and privileges to grant access to its features in Power Automate.

claims.claim: The JSON authoring article includes a validation checklist.
claims.quote: Validation checklist: Before submitting your configuration, review this list. The server runs every check before opening a single byte of data.

claims.claim: Microsoft states no further arrival default beyond the documented maker-selectable data source.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate normalized schema import licensing capacity price meter scheduled incremental refresh default; "normalized" "process mining" "disable". Read roadmap and both normalized guides: maker selection is documented; no further arrival default is stated.

claims.claim: No source says existing processes change if nobody adopts normalized import.
claims.quote: Searched: "normalized" "process mining" scheduled incremental refresh; "normalized" "process mining" "disable". Read roadmap and normalized UX and authoring guides: a new import path is described, not automatic conversion or changes to existing processes.

claims.claim: The JSON configuration maps physical columns to logical Process Mining attributes.
claims.quote: miningMetadata.ImportConfiguration.Attributes answers "What does each column mean to Process Mining?" It maps physical columns (or joined columns from lookup tables) to logical roles
